app.title: Oligo Analyzer Pro
app.summary: A person pastes one DNA primer (5' to 3') and presses Analyze, or uploads a FASTA or text file holding many records. For a single sequence, the interface shows its melting temperature, GC and AT content and molecular weight as headline numbers, a bar chart of base counts, and its reverse complement ready to copy. For a batch, every record is parsed and measured, then plotted as GC% against melting temperature, coloured by length, so outliers stand out. The person also gets a table of every record with its sequence and reverse complement, which they can download as a CSV report.

task.text: Compute melting temperature, base composition and molecular weight for one primer or a file of primers, check them for outliers, and export the results with reverse complements for ordering.

data.text: Short DNA oligonucleotide sequences, typed in one at a time or read from a multi-record FASTA file, each turned into one row of computed properties.
data.item: a short DNA oligo (primer) sequence, one FASTA record

stage.text: checking designed primers before ordering them

mechanism.text: Two tabs separate a quick single-sequence check (summary numbers, a composition bar chart and a reverse complement) from batch processing, where an uploaded FASTA file feeds a GC%-against-Tm scatter plot and a full results table. The table downloads as a CSV.

field.text: oligonucleotide primer property calculation in molecular biology

workflow.name: compute properties for each sequence and export a table of them

steps.here: paste one 5'→3' sequence and press Analyze, or upload a .fasta or .txt file with many records; the file is parsed record by record using its header lines

steps.step: compute a value from the data
steps.here: for each sequence, Tm comes from the Wallace rule, plus GC%, AT%, base counts and single-stranded molecular weight; a pasted sequence with characters other than A, T, G, C or N gets an error, and such records in a file are skipped
a single sequence shows four metric cards (Tm with a 55–60 °C target note), a nucleotide composition bar chart, and its reverse complement in a copyable code block

steps.step: look over every item at a glance
steps.here: a batch is plotted as GC% against Tm, coloured by length, to spot primers with extreme values
a data table lists each record's ID, length, Tm, GC%, AT%, MW, sequence and reverse complement; Download Report saves it as oligo_batch_results.csv

distinctive: Melting temperature uses the Wallace rule (2 °C per A/T, 4 °C per G/C), which suits short oligos
Every sequence gets its reverse complement, so the output can go straight into an oligo order
Molecular weight is summed from per-base weights, with a correction for the missing 5' phosphate
Recommended Tm and GC% ranges appear only as guidance text and the outlier scatter plot; no sequence is flagged automatically

parts.title: Single Sequence tab
parts.summary: A text box and Analyze button for checking one pasted primer, which shows an error if it has invalid characters.

parts.title: Primer metrics
parts.summary: Four headline numbers for the sequence: Wallace-rule melting temperature with a target note, GC content, AT content and molecular weight.

parts.title: Nucleotide composition
parts.summary: A bar chart of A, T, G and C counts in the sequence.

parts.title: Reverse complement
parts.summary: Shows the sequence's reverse complement in a copyable block, ready for ordering.

parts.title: Bulk Analysis tab
parts.summary: Takes an uploaded FASTA or text file, splits it into records by header line, and computes metrics and a reverse complement for each valid record.

parts.title: Batch Quality Control plot
parts.summary: Plots every record as GC% against Tm, coloured by length, so primers with extreme values stand out.

parts.title: Data table and report download
parts.summary: Lists every record's ID, properties, sequence and reverse complement, and downloads them as a CSV report.
